the-plague

Death, a skeleton on a winged creature, swoops over a plague-stricken city in this chilling painting. Arnold Böcklin made two versions in 1898, in the years after great epidemics had struck cities across Europe.
dance-of-death-at-hrastovlje

Skeletons lead a long line of kings, bishops, merchants and peasants toward the grave in this wall painting in a tiny church in Slovenia. John of Kastav painted it in 1490 in the years after the Black Death, when the Dance of Death was a favorite subject.
the-siege-of-constantinople-1453

Ottoman ships crowd the water around the walled city of Constantinople in this manuscript painting of the siege of 1453. Jean Le Tavernier painted it for a Burgundian duke only a few years after the city fell.
sultan-mehmed-ii

Mehmed II conquered Constantinople in 1453 when he was only 21, and later he asked Venice to send a painter to his court. Gentile Bellini painted this portrait of the sultan in 1480 and framed him in a fancy arch.
the-gates-of-constantinople

Sultan Mehmed II rides in triumph through the gates of Constantinople after its fall in 1453, with red banners overhead. The Italian painter Fausto Zonaro, who worked for the Ottoman court, painted it in 1903.
the-conquest-of-constantinople

The Ottoman army marches toward Constantinople in 1453 in a painting by Fausto Zonaro, an Italian artist who worked for the Ottoman sultans. The city fell after a siege of 53 days, ending the Byzantine Empire.
belisarius-begging-for-alms-jacques-louis

Belisarius, the great general of the Byzantine emperor Justinian, is said in a legend to have ended his life blind and begging, and here a soldier who once served under him recognizes him. Jacques-Louis David painted it in 1781, and it made him famous.
the-fall-of-constantinople

A Greek folk-style painting shows the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople in 1453 like a map, with soldiers and ships all around the city. Panagiotis Zographos made it in the 1830s as part of a series for a Greek general who had fought for independence.
the-siege-of-constantinople

Ottoman soldiers with ladders and cannon storm the walls in this French manuscript painting of the fall of Constantinople in 1453, made only a few years afterward. Philippe de Mazerolles painted it around 1460.
empress-zoe-and-constantine-ix-hagia-sophia

In a golden mosaic in the church of Hagia Sophia, the Byzantine Empress Zoe and her husband Constantine IX stand on each side of Christ and offer gifts. It was made in the 1000s, when Constantinople was one of the richest cities on Earth.
the-deesis-mosaic-hagia-sophia

Christ looks out from the Deësis mosaic of Hagia Sophia, with the Virgin Mary and John the Baptist on either side. It was probably made around 1261, when the Byzantines recaptured Constantinople, and is thought to be one of the finest mosaics in the world.
the-comnenus-mosaic-hagia-sophia

The Virgin Mary and Child with the Emperor John II Komnenos and the Empress Irene, in a glittering golden mosaic in Hagia Sophia made around 1118. Byzantine emperors liked to show themselves offering gifts to holy figures.
interior-of-the-hagia-sophia

John Singer Sargent paints the soaring inside of the great church of Hagia Sophia, built by Justinian in 537 and turned into a mosque after the Ottoman conquest of 1453. He painted it on a trip to Istanbul in 1891.
the-fountain-of-the-gate-of-the-old-seraglio-constantin

A domed fountain stands at the gate of the old palace of the Ottoman sultans in Constantinople, in a drawing by the English artist John Frederick Lewis, who traveled through the Ottoman capital in the 1830s and 1840s.
mona-lisa

The Mona Lisa's soft, mysterious smile and misty background make her the most famous painting in the world. Leonardo da Vinci worked on it from around 1503 and kept it with him until he died; today it hangs in the Louvre, where millions come to see it.
the-last-supper-leonardo-da-vi

Leonardo painted the moment Jesus tells his twelve friends that one of them will betray him, and each gesture shows a different reaction. He painted it on a wall in Milan in about 1495–1498 and used perspective to draw every line toward Jesus.
the-creation-of-adam

God stretches out a finger toward Adam, and the tiny gap between their hands has become one of the most famous images ever. Michelangelo painted it in 1512 as part of the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel.
the-birth-of-venus-sandro-bottice

The goddess Venus arrives on the shore on a giant seashell, blown by the winds, in Botticelli's most famous painting of about 1485. It was made for the Medici family of Florence and shows how Renaissance artists were reviving ancient myths.
vitruvian-man

Leonardo's famous drawing of a man with arms and legs stretched inside a circle and a square shows the ideal human proportions described by the Roman architect Vitruvius. It captures the Renaissance idea that humans are the center of the universe, and the drawing is about 1490.
portrait-of-niccolo-machiavelli
Niccolò Machiavelli was a Florentine thinker who wrote The Prince, a book about how rulers really get and keep power. Santi di Tito painted this famous portrait of him about 60 years after his death.
portrait-of-cosimo-the-elder

Cosimo de' Medici the Elder was the banker who made his family the rulers of Florence, and he paid for libraries, churches and artists. Pontormo painted this portrait around 1519, 55 years after Cosimo died.
adoration-of-the-magi

Botticelli painted the Three Kings visiting Jesus and gave the kings the faces of the Medici family, the rulers of Florence, and put himself in the crowd. He painted it around 1475, a glimpse of how rich Renaissance patrons liked to be shown.
portrait-of-girolamo-savonarola

Girolamo Savonarola was a fiery preacher who held Florence in his grip in the 1490s, burning books, mirrors and paintings in his Bonfire of the Vanities. His friend, the painter Fra Bartolomeo, painted him in 1498, the year he was executed.
the-execution-of-girolamo-savonarola

Girolamo Savonarola, the preacher who ruled Florence for a few years, is hanged and burned in the main square in 1498 after losing the support of the people. This painting was made not long after, and shows the whole square from above.
lady-with-an-ermine

A young woman, Cecilia Gallerani, holds a white ermine, which was a symbol of purity, in one of Leonardo's few portraits of a woman. He painted it in about 1490 for the court of Milan, and the way she turns her head makes the picture feel alive.
dante-in-verona

The poet Dante, in exile from Florence, passes some women in Verona while they whisper that he has been to hell, a joke on his great poem the Inferno. Antonio Cotti painted this famous scene in 1879, long after the Renaissance he helped start.
christopher-columbus-at-the-gates-of-the-monastery-of-s

Christopher Columbus, poor and worn out, stops with his young son at a monastery in Spain, where a friendly prior helps him get a hearing at the court of Queen Isabella. Benet Mercadé painted this story in 1858.
the-inspiration-of-christopher-columbus
Columbus sits alone beside the sea, lost in dreams of the voyage west that will change the world. José María Obregón, one of Mexico's leading painters, painted it in 1856.
cortes-and-montezuma-at-mexico-city

The Spanish conqueror Hernán Cortés and the Aztec ruler Montezuma meet in the great city of Tenochtitlan in 1519, followed by war. This colorful print was made in the 1890s by the American lithographers Kurz and Allison.
pizarro-seizing-the-inca-of-peru

In 1532 the Spanish conquistador Francisco Pizarro captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa, beginning the Spanish conquest of the Inca empire. John Everett Millais painted this violent scene in 1846, when he was only 17.
the-virgin-of-the-navigators

The Virgin Mary spreads her cloak over sailors, explorers and ships in an altarpiece painted for the Spanish House of Trade in Seville in about 1535. Christopher Columbus is thought to appear among the kneeling figures, and it is one of the first paintings to show the Americas.
namban-screen-the-arrival-of-the-portuguese

A huge Portuguese trading ship sails into a golden Japanese harbor, with people in strange foreign clothes. These folding screens, called Namban, or 'southern barbarian' screens, showed how Japanese people saw the first Europeans, who arrived in 1543. Kanō Naizen painted this one around 1600.
sir-francis-drake
Francis Drake rests his hand on a globe in a portrait celebrating his voyage around the world from 1577 to 1580, the first by an English captain. Marcus Gheeraerts the Younger painted it in 1591.
the-landing-of-henry-hudson
The English explorer Henry Hudson sails up what is now the Hudson River in 1609 and meets the Lenape people on the shore. Robert Walter Weir painted this meeting in 1835.
the-last-voyage-of-henry-hudson

Henry Hudson, his son and a few others sit in a small boat in the icy northern sea after the crew turned against him in 1611 and cast them adrift. They were never seen again. John Collier painted it in 1881.
america-discovered-vespucci-awakens-america

The explorer Amerigo Vespucci stands in front of a woman who stands for America, newly awakened, in an allegorical engraving by Stradanus of about 1589. The continents were named for Vespucci's first name.
portrait-of-a-man-said-to-be-christopher-columbus
This famous portrait is said to show Christopher Columbus, but it was painted by Sebastiano del Piombo in 1519, years after Columbus died, and no one knows what the explorer really looked like.
hernan-cortes

Hernán Cortés, the Spanish conqueror who led the fall of the Aztec empire in 1519 to 1521, in a 19th-century portrait by the Mexican painter José Salomé Pina. His conquest is still a deeply debated chapter of Mexican history.
luther-at-the-diet-of-worms

In 1521 Martin Luther stands in front of the Emperor Charles V in Worms and refuses to take back his writings, saying 'Here I stand.' Anton von Werner painted this scene in 1877 as a founding moment of the Reformation.
portrait-of-martin-luther

Martin Luther, the monk who challenged the Church, in a portrait painted in 1528 by his friend Lucas Cranach the Elder. Cranach painted Luther many times, and his portraits helped spread Luther's face across Europe.
portraits-of-martin-luther-and-philipp-melanchthon

Martin Luther and his friend and fellow reformer Philipp Melanchthon, shown side by side in two matching panels painted by Lucas Cranach the Elder in 1543. Melanchthon was the scholar who organized Luther's ideas.
luther-posting-the-95-theses

According to tradition, on October 31, 1517, Martin Luther nailed his 95 Theses, complaints against the Church's sale of pardons, to the church door in Wittenberg, which launched the Reformation. Historians debate how it happened, but this scene from 1872 is the famous image.
philip-melanchthon
Philipp Melanchthon, the teacher and thinker who became Luther's closest partner in the Reformation, in an engraving by Albrecht Dürer from 1526. Dürer admired Luther's cause.
portrait-of-erasmus-of-rotterdam

Erasmus, the Dutch scholar who wrote with wit about the Church's faults, sits writing in this calm portrait by Hans Holbein the Younger of 1523. Erasmus wanted to reform the Church from inside and never joined Luther.
portrait-of-henry-viii

Henry VIII, in a puffed gold and jeweled jacket, stands with his hands on his hips in this Holbein portrait of 1537. Henry broke with the pope in the 1530s to marry Anne Boleyn and made himself head of the Church of England.
thomas-cranmer

Thomas Cranmer, the Archbishop of Canterbury who helped Henry VIII break with Rome and wrote the English Book of Common Prayer, was burned at the stake in 1556 under Queen Mary. Gerlach Flicke painted this portrait in 1545.
thomas-cromwell

Thomas Cromwell, Henry VIII's chief minister, carried out the king's break with Rome and closed England's monasteries, but he fell from power and was executed in 1540. Holbein painted him in 1533 at the height of his influence.
